'''''Ceramium strictum''''' is a small marine [[red alga]].

==Description==
This alga grows in tufts to a length of no more than 12 cm long. It is densely branched but not completely [[corticate]] appearing to have a banded or collar-like appearance. The apices of the axes are strongly inrolled. The branches do not have spines. [[Rhizoids]] are numerous.<ref name= "Maggs 1993">Maggs, C.A. and Hommersand, M.H. 1993 ''Seaweeds of the British Isles Volume 1 Rhodophyta Part 3A Ceramiales.'' The Natural History Museum, London {{ISBN|0-11-310045-0}}</ref>

==Reproduction==
[[Cystocarp]]s containing [[carpospore|carposporangia]] and [[tetrasporangia]] are borne on the erect thalli.<ref name="Maggs 1993"/>

==Habitat==
[[Epiphytic]] on other algae and [[mussel]]s in the [[littoral]].<ref name="Maggs 1993"/>

==Distribution==
Southern and western coasts of [[England]] and [[Ireland]].<ref name="Maggs 1993"/><ref>Morton, O. 2003. The marine macroalgae of County Donegal, Ireland. ''Bulletin of Irish biogeographical Society'' No. 27 pp.3 - 164</ref> In [[Europe]] from [[Norway]] to [[France]] and the [[Azores]].<ref name="Maggs 1993"/>

==Nomenclature==
The validity of the name ''Ceramium strictum'' is as yet unsure.<ref name="Maggs 1993"/>
